.abuseipdb: AbuseIPDB publishes only HTML docs (https://docs.abuseipdb.com/) and no OpenAPI/Swagger. Common guessed spec URLs return 404/403. The only OpenAPI descriptions found are community-authored ones (api-evangelist/abuseipdb on GitHub), which are not mirrors of a vendor file, and the referenced raw path did not resolve.
.alienvault-otx: AlienVault/LevelBlue OTX publishes no OpenAPI/Swagger for its DirectConnect API (otx.alienvault.com/api/v1). The only references are the HTML docs and the OTX-Python-SDK. /api/openapi.json just serves the SPA HTML.
.azure_sql: Talks to Azure SQL Database through the mssql driver's TDS protocol, not an HTTP API
.graphql: Generic connector: the endpoint and schema are whatever the user configures, so there is no vendor spec to pin
.greynoise: The connector calls the GreyNoise v2 endpoints (/v2/noise/context/{ip}, /v2/noise/quick/{ip}, /v2/riot/{ip}), which GreyNoise deprecated on 2025-07-28. The only official spec is https://api.greynoise.io/v3/openapi.yaml (OpenAPI 3.0.0, info.version 3.0.0), and it contains no /v2 paths. The connector needs to migrate to /v3/ip/{ip} (?quick=true) before it can be validated against that spec.
.inboundWebhook: Inbound webhook receiver with `actions: {}`. It makes no outbound ctx.client requests to any vendor API.
.jenkins: Self-hosted Jenkins at a user-configured base URL. Its remote access API (/job/{name}/api/json, /build, /buildWithParameters, /queue/item/{id}/api/json, ...) is documented only in prose (jenkins.io/doc/book/using/remote-access-api). Jenkins publishes no OpenAPI, and the surface depends on installed plugins.
.mongodb: Talks to MongoDB through its driver's wire protocol, not an HTTP API
.mysql: Talks to MySQL through its driver's wire protocol, not an HTTP API
.solarwinds_platform: Self-hosted SolarWinds Information Service (SWIS) REST endpoint (/SolarWinds/InformationService/v3/Json/Query, /Invoke/{entity}/{verb}, swis:// URIs) at a user-configured URL. It is documented only in the OrionSDK wiki (solarwinds.github.io/OrionSDK/docs/rest) and has no OpenAPI. The schema is SWQL-entity driven.
.ssf: Signs Security Event Tokens (OpenID Shared Signals Framework) locally with a key Kibana manages, through ctx.signJwt. It sends no requests to a vendor API, so there is no spec to pin; the caller delivers the token to the receiver it configures.
.urlvoid: APIVoid/URLVoid's legacy api1000 endpoint (api.urlvoid.com/api1000/{apiKey}/host/{domain}) puts the API key in the path and returns XML. The vendor publishes no OpenAPI/Swagger for it.
